### komando audit
title: Show the audit log: who did what, where, and the result
- flag:since | --since | From when? | Like 2h, 7d, today or 2026-11-07. Leave empty for the newest entries. | today | optional,check
- flag:target | --target | Only for which servers or conns? | Leave empty for everything. |  | optional,free,choices
- flag:failed | --failed | Only what failed or was blocked? | Only actions that failed or were blocked |  | default,choices
- flag:actor | --actor | Only what one person or AI agent did? | Part of the name, like claude or codex. Leave empty for everyone. | claude | optional,check
- flag:command | --command | Only commands that start with this (like exec, svc.) |  |  | optional,advanced,check
- flag:limit | --limit | The newest N entries (0 = all; with --since or --until, all unless given) |  |  | optional,advanced,default,check
- flag:until | --until | Only entries before this time (the same forms as --since) |  |  | optional,advanced,check
### komando audit verify
title: Check that no audit record was changed, added or removed outside komando
### komando cache
title: Caches (Redis, Valkey, memcached): read and change keys
### komando cache get
title: Show a key: its type, time to live and value (any type)
- arg0 | Conn | Which cache? | A Redis, Valkey or Memcached cache from your list. Add one first: komando cache redis add. |  | choices,check
- arg1 | Key | Which key? | Its exact name. `komando cache keys` lists them. | session:42 | check
- flag:limit | --limit | Show at most how many items of a list, set or hash? | Only for keys that hold many items. A plain text key is shown whole. | 100 | optional,default,check
### komando cache info
title: Server summary: version, role, memory, clients, keys, hit rate
- arg0 | Conn | Which cache? | A Redis, Valkey or Memcached cache from your list. Add one first: komando cache redis add. |  | choices,check
- arg1 | Section | Only one part? (leave empty for a short summary) | server, clients, memory, persistence, stats, replication, cpu or keyspace. Empty shows version, memory, clients and hit rate. | memory | optional,check
- flag:all | --all | Show every raw field instead of the summary? | Only when you left the part above empty. |  | default,choices
### komando cache keys
title: List keys matching a pattern (uses SCAN, so a big cache is not blocked)
- arg0 | Conn | Which cache? | A Redis, Valkey or Memcached cache from your list. Add one first: komando cache redis add. |  | choices,check
- arg1 | Pattern | Which keys? (leave empty for all) | A pattern: * matches anything, so session:* is every key that starts with session:. | session:* | optional,check
- flag:limit | --limit | Show at most how many keys? | Big caches hold millions of keys, so keep it small for a first look. | 100 | optional,default,check

### komando cache memcached edit
title: Change a saved memcached cache (only the flags you pass change)
- arg0 | Name | Which cache? | A cache from your list. Add one first: komando cache memcached add. |  | choices,check
- flag:url | --url | New address (URL)? | Like the one you added it with, without the password. Leave empty to keep it. | postgres://app@10.0.0.5:5432/shop | optional,check
- flag:ask-password | --ask-password | Change the password? | Yes makes the command ask for it, hidden, when it runs. It is saved as a saved password, never on the command line. |  | default,choices
- flag:protected | --protected | Can a mistake on it hurt real users or real data? | Yes means komando asks you before every change there, also changes an AI agent wants to make. No takes that away. |  | optional,choices
- flag:via | --via | Reach it through which server or VPN? | The name of a server or VPN in your list, when it only answers inside that network. Leave empty to keep how it is reached now. | bastion | optional,free,choices
- flag:add-group | --add-group | Add it to a group? | A group lets you pick many at once with @name. Leave empty for none. | web | optional,free,choices
- flag:notes | --notes | Any notes to keep with it? | Free text, like who owns it or what runs there. AI agents read it too. Leave empty to keep the old notes. | main shop database | optional,check
- flag:add-tag | --add-tag | Add these tags |  |  | optional,advanced,check
- flag:credential | --credential | What it logs in with |  |  | optional,advanced,check
- flag:label | --label | Label KEY=VALUE |  |  | optional,advanced,check
- flag:login | --login | How the password is used: ask at every connect, a stored one, or none |  |  | optional,advanced,check
- flag:option | --option | An option of this provider, KEY=VALUE |  |  | optional,advanced,check
- flag:rm-group | --rm-group | Take it out of these groups |  |  | optional,advanced,check
- flag:rm-tag | --rm-tag | Remove these tags |  |  | optional,advanced,check
- flag:unset | --unset | Clear these settings: via, credential, notes, protected |  |  | optional,advanced,check

### komando cache memcached raw
title: Send one memcached command and show the reply
- arg0 | Name | Which cache? | A cache from your list. Add one first: komando cache redis add or komando cache memcached add. |  | choices,check
- arg1 | Command | Which Memcached command? | One word, like GET, HGETALL, TTL or EXPIRE. Its arguments come next. | HGETALL | 
- flag:write | --write | May it change data? | No sends only commands known to just read, so nothing can change. Say yes only for SET, DEL, EXPIRE and the like. |  | default,choices
### komando cache memcached remove
title: Forget a saved memcached cache (the cache is not touched)
- arg0 | Target | Which caches should come off your list? | Only komando's list changes; the cache itself is not touched. |  | free,choices,check

- flag:end | --end | End the session a person's login keeps open |  |  | advanced,default,choices

### komando cache set
title: Set a string key, replacing any old value
- arg0 | Conn | Which cache? | A Redis, Valkey or Memcached cache from your list. Add one first: komando cache redis add. |  | choices,check
- arg1 | Key | Which key to set? | Its exact name. An old value under this name is replaced. | feature:dark-mode | check
- arg2 | Value | Which value? | Plain text. Never put a password here; `komando secret set` keeps one. | on | check
- flag:ttl | --ttl | Delete it by itself after how long? (leave empty to keep it) | The key's time to live. Empty keeps it until someone deletes it. | 30m, 24h or 7d | optional,check

### komando cluster
title: Kubernetes and Docker Swarm: check, read logs, roll out, scale
### komando cluster add
title: Add a cluster
- arg0 | Name | Name? |  |  | check
- arg1 | URL | URL? |  |  | check
- flag:ask-password | --ask-password | Type the password now (hidden, a person at a terminal); it is stored in the vault as secret:NAME-pass and used as --password-ref |  |  | advanced,default,choices
- flag:group | --group | Put it in these groups (comma-separated) |  |  | optional,advanced,check
- flag:label | --label | Label KEY=VALUE (repeatable) |  |  | optional,advanced,check
- flag:login | --login | How komando logs in, as show names it: ask (a person types the password at every connect; never stored), password (a stored one: with --ask-password or --password-ref); a server also takes key (with --key or --identity) and agent (ssh-agent and ~/.ssh only), a conn none (no password of komando's own) |  |  | optional,advanced,check
- flag:notes | --notes | Free-form notes (komando conn show shows them to people and agents) |  |  | optional,advanced,check
- flag:option | --option | An option of this kind, KEY=VALUE (repeatable) |  |  | optional,advanced,check
- flag:overwrite | --overwrite | Replace a conn that has the same name |  |  | advanced,default,choices
- flag:password-ref | --password-ref | Where the password is: secret:NAME (saved with komando secret set NAME), env:VAR, file:PATH or a password manager like op://... |  |  | optional,advanced,check
- flag:protected | --protected | Production: komando asks you before every change, and an AI agent needs your yes in a window |  |  | advanced,default,choices
- flag:tag | --tag | Tags, like prod (comma-separated) |  |  | optional,advanced,check
- flag:via | --via | Reach it through these servers (bastions) or a VPN first, comma-separated path; no local port is opened |  |  | optional,advanced,free,choices

- flag:stack | --stack | Swarm only: the stack's name (empty on Kubernetes) | Swarm: the stack name | shop | optional,check
- flag:force-conflicts | --force-conflicts | Kubernetes: take over fields another field manager owns |  |  | advanced,default,choices
- flag:namespace | --namespace | Kubernetes namespace (default: the context's, else default) |  |  | optional,advanced,check
### komando cluster deploy
title: Roll out a new image
- arg0 | Target (clusters) | Which cluster? | A Kubernetes cluster from your list. For a Docker Swarm, type its manager server's name. @group reaches several. |  | free,choices,check
- arg1 | Type/name | Which workload? | Its kind and name, like deployment/api or statefulset/db. komando cluster list shows them. | deployment/api | check
- flag:image | --image | Which image should it run now? | The full image name with its new tag, as in docker pull. | ghcr.io/acme/api:1.4.3 | check
- flag:wait | --wait | Wait until it is done? | Yes: komando stays until every copy runs the new version, or says what went wrong. |  | default,choices
- flag:container | --container | Which container gets the image (needed when there are several) |  |  | optional,advanced,check
- flag:namespace | --namespace | Kubernetes namespace (default: the context's, else default) |  |  | optional,advanced,check

### komando cluster logs

- flag:timestamps | --timestamps | Start each line with its time |  |  | advanced,default,choices

title: Change a conn (only the flags you pass change)
- arg0 | Name | Which conn? | A database, cache, queue, file storage, cluster or registry in your list. |  | choices,check

### komando cp
title: Copy files, written SRC DST with TARGET:PATH (upload/download)
- arg0 | Src | Copy from where? | A file or folder on this computer (./site), or on a server as SERVER:PATH (web1:/var/log/app). | ./site | check
- arg1 | Dst | Copy to where? | SERVER:PATH on servers (@web:/var/www/site for a group), or a folder on this computer (./logs/). | web1:/var/www/site | check
- flag:recursive | --recursive | Is it a folder? (copy everything in it) | Ending the source with / copies what is in the folder, not the folder itself. |  | default,choices
- flag:sudo | --sudo | Run it with sudo (as root)? | Yes for system files, like /etc. Works for single files. |  | default,choices
- flag:continue | --continue | Go on with a copy that was cut off: keep the part already at the destination when it matches the source, send the rest, then check the whole file (sha256) |  |  | advanced,default,choices
- flag:mode | --mode | Upload: file mode, like 0755 |  |  | optional,advanced,check
- flag:overwrite | --overwrite | Download: replace files that already exist on this computer |  |  | advanced,default,choices
- flag:parents | --parents | Upload: create missing parent folders |  |  | advanced,default,choices
- flag:progress | --progress | With -o json, write progress to the error output (stderr), one JSON object per line |  |  | advanced,default,choices
- flag:size | --size | An upload from stdin (-): how many bytes it sends, like 10MiB; a stream of another length replaces nothing (SIZE_CONFLICT) |  |  | optional,advanced,check

### komando db dump
title: Save a copy of a database to a file on this computer (person only)
- arg0 | Conn | Which database should it back up? | A database you added to komando. |  | choices,check
- flag:to | --to | Save the backup to which file on this computer? | A new file; it never overwrites one. Ending in .gz makes it smaller. Only you can read it. Left out: CONN-<date>.sql.gz in this folder. | ./prod-2026-11-10.sql.gz | optional,check
- flag:format | --format | Which kind of backup? | plain is SQL any database tool reads. custom is PostgreSQL's own archive (needs pg_dump on a server; no .gz then). |  | optional,default,choices
- flag:schema-only | --schema-only | Only the tables' shape, without the rows? | Yes saves tables, indexes and functions but no data. |  | default,choices

- flag:run-on | --run-on | Which server should run the backup tool? | A server that has pg_dump or mysqldump and can reach the database. Leave empty to use the server the database is reached through. |  | optional,free,choices
### komando db explain
title: Show how the database would run a query (--analyze runs it and measures)
- arg0 | Conn | Which database? | A database from your list (`komando list kind:db`). Add one with `komando db add`. |  | choices,check
- arg1 | SQL | Which query should it explain? | The SQL you want to make faster. It shows how the database finds the rows (an index or a full scan). | select * from orders where user_id = 42 | check
- flag:analyze | --analyze | Run the query too and measure the real time? | Yes runs it for real, which takes as long as the query. A query that changes data then needs a yes to the next question. |  | default,choices
- flag:write | --write | May it change data? | No runs it read-only, so nothing can change. Say yes only for insert, update, delete or create. |  | default,choices
- flag:arg | --arg | Value for a placeholder ($1 in postgres, ? in mysql/sqlite, @p1 in sqlserver, :1 in oracle, {p1:String} in clickhouse, ? in snowflake and bigquery); repeat in order |  |  | optional,advanced,check
- flag:limit | --limit | The most rows to return per statement (0 = no limit; --max-output caps the size too) |  |  | optional,advanced,default,check
- flag:max-bytes | --max-bytes | BigQuery: the most a query may read, which BigQuery bills by, like 50GB (default 10GB; 0 = no cap) |  |  | optional,advanced,check

title: Edit a file on servers by replacing exact text
- arg0 | Target (servers) | On which server? | Pick one, or type a group like @web to do the same on several. |  | free,choices,check

- flag:mode | --mode | File mode, like 0640 (default: keep existing or 0644) |  |  | optional,advanced,check
- flag:no-follow | --no-follow | Refuse to write through a symbolic link (by default the file it points to is written and the link stays) |  |  | advanced,default,choices
- flag:owner | --owner | Owner[:group] (needs --sudo) |  |  | optional,advanced,check
- flag:parents | --parents | Create missing parent folders |  |  | advanced,default,choices
- flag:regex | --regex | Treat --old as a Go regular expression |  |  | advanced,default,choices
- flag:validate | --validate | Check the new file before it goes into place; %s is its path (like 'visudo -cf %s', 'nginx -t -c %s') |  |  | optional,advanced,check

### komando host
title: Servers in komando's list: add, change, check, remove
### komando host add
title: Add a server to your list
- arg0 | Name | Name? |  |  | check
- arg1 | Address | Address? |  |  | optional,check
- flag:address | --address | Host name or IP address (winrm://USER@HOST for a Windows server over WinRM) |  |  | optional,advanced,check
- flag:ask-password | --ask-password | Type the password now (hidden, a person at a terminal); it is stored in the vault as secret:NAME-pass and used as --password-ref |  |  | advanced,default,choices
- flag:env | --env | Env KEY=VALUE exported before every command (repeatable) |  |  | optional,advanced,check
- flag:group | --group | Put it in these groups (comma-separated) |  |  | optional,advanced,check
- flag:identity | --identity | Path to a private key file |  |  | optional,advanced,check
- flag:key | --key | Name of a key in komando's key list (see komando key list) |  |  | optional,advanced,free,choices
- flag:label | --label | Label KEY=VALUE (repeatable) |  |  | optional,advanced,check
- flag:login | --login | How komando logs in, as show names it: ask (a person types the password at every connect; never stored), password (a stored one: with --ask-password or --password-ref); a server also takes key (with --key or --identity) and agent (ssh-agent and ~/.ssh only), a conn none (no password of komando's own) |  |  | optional,advanced,check
- flag:notes | --notes | Free-form notes (komando host show shows them to people and agents) |  |  | optional,advanced,check
- flag:os | --os | The server's OS: windows (commands run in PowerShell) or linux (the default, also for other Unixes) |  |  | optional,advanced,check
- flag:overwrite | --overwrite | Replace a server that has the same name |  |  | advanced,default,choices
- flag:password-ref | --password-ref | Where the password is: secret:NAME (saved with komando secret set NAME), env:VAR, file:PATH or a password manager like op://... |  |  | optional,advanced,check
- flag:port | --port | SSH port (default 22) |  |  | optional,advanced,check
- flag:protected | --protected | Production: komando asks you before every change, and an AI agent needs your yes in a window |  |  | advanced,default,choices
- flag:proxy-command | --proxy-command | A command on this computer that carries the connection (OpenSSH ProxyCommand; %h %p %r) |  |  | optional,advanced,check
- flag:ssm | --ssm | Reach it through AWS Systems Manager: the address is the instance ID (komando speaks Session Manager itself when the aws CLI or its plugin is not installed) |  |  | advanced,default,choices
- flag:sudo-ref | --sudo-ref | Where the sudo password is, written like --password-ref |  |  | optional,advanced,check
- flag:tag | --tag | Tags, like prod (comma-separated) |  |  | optional,advanced,check
- flag:user | --user | The user to log in as |  |  | optional,advanced,check
- flag:via | --via | Reach it through these servers (bastions) or a VPN first, comma-separated path, like vpn1,bastion |  |  | optional,advanced,free,choices
### komando host ca
title: Trust servers through the CA that signs their host keys
### komando host ca add
title: Trust a CA for the servers its patterns match (person only)
- arg0 | Name | A short name for this CA? |  | corp | check
- flag:key | --key | The CA's public key file (.pub)? | Check its fingerprint with the people who run the CA first: it will vouch for every server it signs. | ~/corp-ca.pub | optional,free,choices
- flag:hosts | --hosts | Which server names may it vouch for? | Name at least the domain: *.corp.example or 10.1.2.*. A lone * is refused. | *.corp.example | optional,check
- flag:from | --from | Or read a known_hosts file's @cert-authority lines? | A known_hosts file: read its @cert-authority and @revoked lines | ~/.ssh/known_hosts | optional,check

### komando host edit
title: Change one or more servers (only the flags you pass change)
- arg0 | Target (servers) | Which servers? | Pick one from your list, or type @group, tag:prod or several names separated by spaces or commas. |  | free,choices,check
- flag:address | --address | New address? | The server's IP address or host name. Leave empty to keep it. | 203.0.113.20 | optional,check
- flag:user | --user | New login user? | The user name you log in with. Leave empty to keep it. | deploy | optional,check
- flag:port | --port | New SSH port? | Usually 22. Leave empty to keep it. | 2222 | optional,check
- flag:ask-password | --ask-password | Change the password? | Yes makes the command ask for it, hidden, when it runs. It is saved as a saved password, never on the command line. |  | default,choices
- flag:key | --key | Log in with which key from komando's key list? | `komando key list` shows them. Leave empty to keep how it logs in now. |  | optional,free,choices
- flag:protected | --protected | Can a mistake on it hurt real users or real data? | Yes means komando asks you before every change there, also changes an AI agent wants to make. No takes that away. |  | optional,choices
- flag:via | --via | Reach it through which server or VPN? | The name of a server or VPN in your list, when it only answers inside that network. Leave empty to keep how it is reached now. | bastion | optional,free,choices
- flag:add-group | --add-group | Add it to a group? | A group lets you pick many at once with @name. Leave empty for none. | web | optional,free,choices
- flag:notes | --notes | Any notes to keep with it? | Free text, like who owns it or what runs there. AI agents read it too. Leave empty to keep the old notes. | main shop database | optional,check
- flag:add-tag | --add-tag | Add these tags (comma-separated) |  |  | optional,advanced,check
- flag:env | --env | Set KEY=VALUE, exported before every command (an empty value removes it; repeatable) |  |  | optional,advanced,check
- flag:forward-agent | --forward-agent | Lend the server your ssh-agent while komando is connected (root there can use your keys then; asks first) |  |  | advanced,default,choices
- flag:identity | --identity | Path to a private key file |  |  | optional,advanced,check
- flag:label | --label | Set label KEY=VALUE (an empty value removes it) |  |  | optional,advanced,check
- flag:login | --login | How komando logs in, as show names it: ask (a person types the password at every connect; never stored), password (a stored one: with --ask-password or --password-ref); a server also takes key (with --key or --identity) and agent (ssh-agent and ~/.ssh only), a conn none (no password of komando's own) |  |  | optional,advanced,check
- flag:os | --os | The server's OS: windows (commands run in PowerShell) or linux (the default, also for other Unixes) |  |  | optional,advanced,check
- flag:password-ref | --password-ref | Where the password is: secret:NAME (saved with komando secret set NAME), env:VAR, file:PATH or a password manager like op://... |  |  | optional,advanced,check
- flag:proxy-command | --proxy-command | A command on this computer that carries the connection (OpenSSH ProxyCommand; %h %p %r) |  |  | optional,advanced,check
- flag:rm-group | --rm-group | Take it out of these groups |  |  | optional,advanced,check
- flag:rm-tag | --rm-tag | Remove these tags |  |  | optional,advanced,check
- flag:ssm | --ssm | Reach it through AWS Systems Manager: the address is the instance ID (komando speaks Session Manager itself when the aws CLI or its plugin is not installed) |  |  | advanced,default,choices
- flag:sudo-ref | --sudo-ref | Where the sudo password is, written like --password-ref |  |  | optional,advanced,check
- flag:unset | --unset | Clear these settings: user,key,identity,password-ref,sudo-ref,via,proxy-command,notes,port,protected,forward-agent,os,transport (transport: back to SSH from WinRM) |  |  | optional,advanced,check

### komando job

### komando job kill
title: Stop a job: send a signal to its process group (default TERM)
- arg0 | Job | Which job? | A job started with `komando job start`. `komando job list` shows them. |  | free,choices,check
- flag:signal | --signal | How should it stop? | TERM asks it to stop and clean up. KILL stops it at once, use it when TERM did not work. |  | optional,default,choices
- flag:sudo | --sudo | Was the job started with sudo? | Then stopping it needs sudo too. |  | default,choices
### komando job list
title: List the jobs komando started (--refresh asks the servers)
- flag:target | --target | Only the jobs on which servers? | Leave empty for every job komando knows. |  | optional,free,choices
- flag:refresh | --refresh | Ask the servers whether each job still runs? | No shows what komando saw last time, which is quicker. |  | default,choices
- flag:limit | --limit | Show at most this many jobs, newest first (0 = all) |  |  | optional,advanced,check

### komando job start
title: Start a background job on each server TARGET picks
- arg0 | Target (servers) | Which servers? | Pick one from your list, or type @group, tag:prod or several names separated by spaces or commas. |  | free,choices,check
- arg1 | Command | What command should it run? | A long task that keeps running when your connection drops. Type it as you would on the server. | apt-get -y upgrade | 
- flag:sudo | --sudo | Run it with sudo (as root)? | Say yes when it needs admin rights, like changing system files or services. |  | default,choices
- flag:read-only | --read-only | Does it only look, without changing anything? | Yes lets it run on a production server without asking you first. Say yes only when that is true. |  | default,choices
- flag:dir | --dir | In which folder on the server should it run? | Leave empty for the login user's home folder. | /srv/app | optional,check
- flag:arg | --arg | With --script: an argument for the script, $1 ... (repeatable) |  |  | optional,advanced,check
- flag:env | --env | Export KEY=VALUE before the command (repeatable) |  |  | optional,advanced,check
- flag:interpreter | --interpreter | With --script: the interpreter on the server (default: from the #! line, else sh) |  |  | optional,advanced,check
- flag:script | --script | Run this script from this computer as the job ('-' = komando's stdin) |  |  | optional,advanced,check
- flag:stdin-file | --stdin-file | Send this file on this computer as the command's input ('-' = komando's stdin) |  |  | optional,advanced,check
- flag:sudo-user | --sudo-user | Run as this user with sudo -u |  |  | optional,advanced,check

### komando key
title: SSH keys: make, add, put on servers, take off
### komando key add
title: Add a private key file you already have (komando keeps its path)
- arg0 | Name | What name should the key have in komando? | Letters, digits, dot, dash and underscore, starting with a letter or digit. | personal | check
- arg1 | File | Where is the private key file on this computer? | The file without .pub at the end. It stays where it is. ~/ means your home folder. | ~/.ssh/id_ed25519 | check
- flag:passphrase-ref | --passphrase-ref | Where is the key's passphrase kept? | Only for a key that has a passphrase. Store it first with `komando secret set NAME` (it asks hidden), then type secret:NAME here. Leave empty for a key without one. | secret:work-key-pass | optional,check
- flag:cert | --cert | An OpenSSH user certificate for the key (default: FILE-cert.pub next to it, if there) |  |  | optional,advanced,check
### komando key deploy
title: Install a public key in ~/.ssh/authorized_keys (like ssh-copy-id)
- arg0 | Name | Which key? | One of your komando SSH keys, or type the path of a .pub file on this computer. | ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub | free,choices,check
- arg1 | Target (servers) | On which servers? | Pick one from your list, or type @group, tag:prod or several names separated by spaces or commas. |  | free,choices,check
- flag:set-default | --set-default | Should komando log in with this key from now on? | Yes switches each server where it worked to this key. |  | default,choices
### komando key edit

- arg0 | Name | Which key? | One of your komando SSH keys. `komando key list` shows them. |  | choices,check

- flag:cert | --cert | An OpenSSH user certificate for the key |  |  | optional,advanced,check
- flag:unset | --unset | Clear this setting: passphrase-ref, cert |  |  | optional,advanced,check
### komando key gen
title: Make a new SSH key pair (ed25519 by default)
- arg0 | Name | What name should the new key have? | Letters, digits, dot, dash and underscore, starting with a letter or digit. Next, `komando key deploy` puts it on your servers. | deploy | check
- flag:type | --type | Which kind of key? | ed25519 is short and safe; pick rsa only for an old server that does not take ed25519. |  | optional,default,choices
- flag:bits | --bits | Key size: RSA 3072-16384 (default 4096), ECDSA 256|384|521 |  |  | optional,advanced,check
- flag:comment | --comment | Public key comment (default komando-NAME) |  |  | optional,advanced,check

### komando logs
title: Read logs from journald, a file or a container
- arg0 | Target (servers) | Which server? | Pick one from your list, or type @group, tag:prod or several names separated by spaces or commas. |  | free,choices,check
- flag:unit | --unit | Which service's log? | A systemd service, like nginx or ssh. Leave empty to read a file, a container or the whole system journal. | nginx | optional,check
- flag:file | --file | Or which log file? | The full path of a log file on the server. Leave empty for the system journal or a container. | /var/log/nginx/error.log | optional,show,check
- flag:container | --container | Or which Docker container? | Its name or ID. Leave empty for the whole system journal. | api | optional,show,check
- flag:since | --since | From how long ago? | 30m or 2h means that long ago; the journal (a service or the whole system) also takes today or 2026-01-02 10:00. Leave empty for the latest lines. | 1h | optional,show,check
- flag:until | --until | Up to when? | Like 10m (ten minutes ago), or a time like 2026-01-02 11:00. Leave empty for up to now. | 10m | optional,show,check
- flag:grep | --grep | Only lines that contain a word? | Big and small letters count the same. Several words: error|fail. Leave empty for every line. | error | optional,check
- flag:sudo | --sudo | Read with sudo (as root)? | Say yes for the whole system journal or a log file only root may read. |  | default,choices
- flag:follow | --follow | Keep printing new lines until Ctrl-C |  |  | advanced,default,choices
- flag:limit | --limit | The most lines to show (the last ones) |  |  | optional,advanced,default,check
- flag:priority | --priority | Journal priority and worse: emerg, alert, crit, err, warning, notice, info, debug (or 0-7) |  |  | optional,advanced,check
- flag:timestamps | --timestamps | Show when each container log line was written (containers) |  |  | advanced,default,choices

### komando policy

### komando policy check

- arg0 | Regex | Which command should komando block? | Like kubectl delete: write it as kubectl\s+delete (\s+ means spaces, .* means anything). Then check it with komando policy check "kubectl delete pod web". | kubectl\s+delete | check

- arg0 | Rule | Which rule? | Its id: `komando policy list` shows them. | docker-prune | check

- flag:add-server | --add-server | Only on which servers? | Leave empty to switch it off on every server. |  | optional,free,choices,show
- flag:add-group | --add-group | With --off: only on the servers in these groups as they are now |  |  | optional,advanced,check
- flag:rm-group | --rm-group | Switch the rule on again on the servers these groups named |  |  | optional,advanced,check
- flag:rm-server | --rm-server | Switch the rule on again on these servers |  |  | optional,advanced,check

### komando queue create
title: Create a topic, queue or stream
- arg0 | Conn | Which message queue? | A Kafka, RabbitMQ, NATS, SQS or Pub/Sub queue from your list. Add one with Add, Queues. |  | choices,check
- arg1 | Topic | What should the new topic or queue be called? | Pub/Sub: subscriptions/NAME makes a subscription; then give its topic below as topic=NAME. An SQS name ending in .fifo makes a FIFO queue. | orders | check
- flag:partitions | --partitions | Kafka only: how many partitions? | More partitions let more readers work at once. Empty uses the brokers' default. | 6 | optional,check
- flag:replicas | --replicas | Kafka and NATS: how many copies? | 3 keeps the data when a server fails. Empty uses the default. | 3 | optional,check
- flag:type | --type | RabbitMQ only: which queue type? | quorum keeps copies on several nodes. Empty uses the server's default. |  | optional,choices
- flag:config | --config | Any settings? (KEY=VALUE) | Kafka retention.ms=..., RabbitMQ x-max-length=..., NATS max_age=7d, SQS VisibilityTimeout=60, Pub/Sub topic=orders. Empty for none. | retention.ms=604800000 | optional,check

### komando vpn
title: VPNs komando connects when a path needs one: add, connect, check
### komando vpn add
title: Add a VPN
- arg0 | Name | Name? |  |  | check
- arg1 | Kind | Kind? |  |  | check
- flag:allow-pap | --allow-pap | L2TP: let the server pick a login that does not prove it is the server: PAP, which hands it your password itself, CHAP-MD5 or none (needs a person's yes) |  |  | advanced,default,choices
- flag:ask-password | --ask-password | Type the password now (hidden, a person at a terminal); it is stored in the vault as secret:NAME-pass and used as --password-ref |  |  | advanced,default,choices
- flag:ask-psk | --ask-psk | L2TP, IPsec, IKEv2: type the pre-shared key now (hidden, a person at a terminal); it is stored in the vault as secret:NAME-psk and used as --psk-ref |  |  | advanced,default,choices
- flag:ca | --ca | IKEv2: the CA certificate (PEM) that signed the server's certificate, if not a public one |  |  | optional,advanced,check
- flag:check | --check | Host:port reachable only through this VPN (vpn up and test connect to it; needed for system and openvpn) |  |  | optional,advanced,check
- flag:config | --config | WireGuard: the .conf file; OpenVPN: the .ovpn file (both kept in the vault) |  |  | optional,advanced,check
- flag:group | --group | Put it in these groups (comma-separated) |  |  | optional,advanced,check
- flag:id | --id | IPsec: the group name; IKEv2: your identity (default: --user, or your address) |  |  | optional,advanced,check
- flag:label | --label | Label KEY=VALUE (repeatable) |  |  | optional,advanced,check
- flag:legacy-crypto | --legacy-crypto | L2TP, IPsec: also offer 3DES and DH groups 2 and 5, for old servers (weak; needs a person's yes) |  |  | advanced,default,choices
- flag:mfa | --mfa | The login needs a person (MFA, SSO): only 'vpn up' run by a person connects it |  |  | advanced,default,choices
- flag:notes | --notes | Free-form notes |  |  | optional,advanced,check
- flag:overwrite | --overwrite | Replace a VPN with the same name |  |  | advanced,default,choices
- flag:password-ref | --password-ref | Where the password is (Tailscale: the auth key): secret:NAME (saved with komando secret set NAME), env:VAR, file:PATH or a password manager like op://... |  |  | optional,advanced,check
- flag:portal | --portal | GlobalProtect, Fortinet, AnyConnect, Pulse, F5: the VPN server or portal |  |  | optional,advanced,check
- flag:protected | --protected | Komando asks a person before it changes or removes this VPN; an AI agent needs their yes in a window |  |  | advanced,default,choices
- flag:proxy-address | --proxy-address | SOCKS: host:port of the proxy; proxy: host:port or http(s)://host:port |  |  | optional,advanced,check
- flag:psk-ref | --psk-ref | L2TP, IPsec, IKEv2: the pre-shared key (IPsec: the group password), as a reference like --password-ref |  |  | optional,advanced,check
- flag:remote-id | --remote-id | IKEv2: the server's identity, if not its --server name |  |  | optional,advanced,check
- flag:server | --server | L2TP, IPsec, IKEv2: the VPN server (host or host:port); Tailscale: a Headscale login server URL |  |  | optional,advanced,check
- flag:service | --service | System VPN: its name in your computer's settings, so 'vpn up' can connect it |  |  | optional,advanced,check
- flag:tag | --tag | Tags, like prod (comma-separated) |  |  | optional,advanced,check
- flag:user | --user | User name for the VPN login |  |  | optional,advanced,check

### komando vpn edit
title: Change one or more VPNs (only the flags you pass change)
- arg0 | Target (VPNs) | Which VPN? | One from your list. `komando vpn list` shows them. |  | free,choices,check
- flag:check | --check | Which address can only be reached through this VPN? | An address and port inside the private network. komando connects to it to see that the VPN works. Leave empty to keep it. | 10.0.0.5:22 | optional,check
- flag:user | --user | New user name for the VPN login? | Leave empty to keep it. | alice | optional,check
- flag:password-ref | --password-ref | Where is the new password kept? | Store it first with `komando secret set NAME` (it asks hidden), then type secret:NAME here. Leave empty to keep it. | secret:office-pass | optional,check
- flag:notes | --notes | Notes about this VPN? | Anything to remember. Leave empty to keep them. | office in Jakarta, ask Budi for access | optional,check
- flag:add-group | --add-group | Put it in these groups (comma-separated) |  |  | optional,advanced,check
- flag:add-tag | --add-tag | Add these tags (comma-separated) |  |  | optional,advanced,check
- flag:allow-pap | --allow-pap | L2TP: let the server pick a login that does not prove it is the server: PAP, which hands it your password itself, CHAP-MD5 or none (turning it on needs a person's yes) |  |  | advanced,default,choices
- flag:ca | --ca | IKEv2: the CA certificate (PEM) that signed the server's certificate; "" for a public one |  |  | optional,advanced,check
- flag:id | --id | IPsec: the group name; IKEv2: your identity |  |  | optional,advanced,check
- flag:label | --label | Set label KEY=VALUE (an empty value removes it) |  |  | optional,advanced,check
- flag:legacy-crypto | --legacy-crypto | L2TP, IPsec: also offer 3DES and DH groups 2 and 5, for old servers (weak; turning it on needs a person's yes) |  |  | advanced,default,choices
- flag:mfa | --mfa | The login needs a person (MFA, SSO) |  |  | advanced,default,choices
- flag:portal | --portal | GlobalProtect, Fortinet, AnyConnect, Pulse, F5: the VPN server or portal |  |  | optional,advanced,check
- flag:protected | --protected | Komando asks a person before it changes or removes this VPN; an AI agent needs their yes in a window |  |  | advanced,default,choices
- flag:proxy-address | --proxy-address | SOCKS: host:port of the proxy; proxy: host:port or http(s)://host:port |  |  | optional,advanced,check
- flag:psk-ref | --psk-ref | L2TP, IPsec, IKEv2: the pre-shared key (IPsec: the group password) |  |  | optional,advanced,check
- flag:remote-id | --remote-id | IKEv2: the server's identity |  |  | optional,advanced,check
- flag:rm-group | --rm-group | Take it out of these groups |  |  | optional,advanced,check
- flag:rm-tag | --rm-tag | Remove these tags |  |  | optional,advanced,check
- flag:server | --server | L2TP, IPsec, IKEv2: the VPN server |  |  | optional,advanced,check
- flag:service | --service | System VPN: its name in your computer's settings |  |  | optional,advanced,check
- flag:unset | --unset | Clear these settings: user,password-ref,psk-ref,id,remote-id,ca,check,notes |  |  | optional,advanced,check

### komando vpn test
title: Check that VPNs connect
- arg0 | Target (VPNs) | Which VPN should be tested? | komando connects through it and says whether it works. |  | choices,check
- flag:wait | --wait | Keep trying for how long? | Like 30s or 5m: it tests again every few seconds until it works. Leave empty to test once. | 5m | optional,check
- flag:end | --end | End the kept sessions of the servers named (every server when none is named), instead of testing |  |  | advanced,default,choices
### komando vpn up
title: Connect a VPN now and keep it up
- arg0 | Name | Which VPN should connect? | It stays up for later commands. When it asks for a login or a code, type it here. |  | choices,check
### add form: Server / Server
title: Add a server
- name | Name | What do you want to call this server? | A short name you type later, like komando test web1. Letters, digits, dot, dash, underscore. | web1 | check
- address | Address | What is the server's address? | Its IP address or host name, from your hosting panel or cloud console. | 203.0.113.20 or vps.example.com | addr,check
- user | User | Which user do you log in as? | The login name on the server. Many VPS use root; Ubuntu cloud servers use ubuntu; Windows uses Administrator, or user@domain for a domain user. | root | default,check
- os | System | What does the server run? | Windows servers run commands in PowerShell; everything else is treated like Linux. |  | default,choices
- transport | Connection | How does komando reach this Windows server? | Not sure? Ask whoever runs it. WinRM is often on already, as Ansible uses it; OpenSSH also gives shell and tunnels. |  | default,choices,show
- port | Port | Which SSH port does it use? | Almost always 22. Change it only if your provider gave you another number. |  | default,show,check
- winrmtls | Encryption | How does WinRM encrypt the connection? | Pick the first unless komando test says the certificate is not trusted. A certificate from your company's CA: keep the first and see https://github.com/sgnd/komando/blob/main/docs/features/windows.md. |  | default,choices,show
- winrmport | Port | Which WinRM port does it use? | Almost always 5986 for HTTPS and 5985 for HTTP. |  | default,show,check
- login | Login | How do you log in? | Not sure? Pick the first: komando tries your keys and asks for a password if none works. |  | default,choices,show
- identity | Key file | Where is the key file? | The private key file, often ending in .pem. Not the .pub file. | ~/Downloads/my-vps.pem | show,check
- key | Key | Which of your komando keys? |  |  | choices,show
- protected | Production | Can a mistake on this server hurt real users or real data? | Production: komando asks you before every change, and an AI agent needs your yes in a window. |  | default,choices
- via | Jump host | Through another server (a jump host)? | Pick a server or VPN when this server only answers from inside that network. |  | advanced,default,choices
- code | One-time code | Does it also ask for a one-time code when you log in? | A 6-digit code from an app like Google Authenticator. Most servers do not. |  | advanced,default,choices,show
- group | Group | Put it in a group? | A group lets one command reach many, like komando test @web. Empty for none. | web | optional,advanced,check
- notes | Notes | Any notes for later? | Free text, shown in komando show and to AI agents. Never put a password here. |  | optional,advanced
### add form: Databases / PostgreSQL
title: Add a PostgreSQL database
- name | Name | What do you want to call this database? | A short name you type later, like komando test app-db. Letters, digits, dot, dash, underscore. | app-db | check
- via | Reached | How does this computer reach the database? | Many databases only answer on their own server: then pick that server. |  | default,choices,when
- host | Address | What is the database server's address? | Through a server, 127.0.0.1 means that server itself. Through a VPN, type its address inside the VPN's network. | 10.0.0.5 or db.example.com | addr,default,check
- port | Port | Which port does it listen on? | The usual PostgreSQL port is 5432. |  | default,check
- user | User | Which database user do you log in with? | The user name the database knows you by, not your SSH user. | app | 
- database | Database | Which database inside the server? | One server holds several databases. Empty uses the server's default. | app | optional
- password | Password | Does this user log in with a password? | Almost always yes. komando asks for it after this, hidden, and keeps it as a saved password. |  | default,choices
- protected | Production | Can a mistake on this database hurt real users or real data? | Production: komando asks you before every change, and an AI agent needs your yes in a window. |  | default,choices
- tls | Encryption | How should the connection be encrypted? | Leave it to komando unless the server has no TLS or a certificate it made itself. |  | advanced,default,choices
- group | Group | Put it in a group? | A group lets one command reach many, like komando test @web. Empty for none. | web | optional,advanced,check
- notes | Notes | Any notes for later? | Free text, shown in komando show and to AI agents. Never put a password here. |  | optional,advanced

### add form: Databases / Oracle Database
title: Add an Oracle database
- name | Name | What do you want to call this database? | A short name you type later, like komando test erp-db. Letters, digits, dot, dash, underscore. | erp-db | check

- sid | SID | What is the SID? | The instance name, as ORACLE_SID on the database server. | ORCL | show,check
- user | User | Which database user do you log in with? | In Oracle a user is also a schema. komando asks for the password after this, hidden. | app | check
- protected | Production | Can a mistake on this database hurt real users or real data? | Production: komando asks you before every change, and an AI agent needs your yes in a window. |  | default,choices
- tls | Encryption | How should the connection be encrypted? | Leave it to komando unless the server has no TLS or a certificate it made itself. |  | advanced,default,choices
- group | Group | Put it in a group? | A group lets one command reach many, like komando test @web. Empty for none. | web | optional,advanced,check
- notes | Notes | Any notes for later? | Free text, shown in komando show and to AI agents. Never put a password here. |  | optional,advanced

- database | Database | Which database should commands use? | Empty uses the user's default database. | analytics | optional,check
- password | Password | Does this user log in with a password? | Almost always yes. komando asks for it after this, hidden, and keeps it as a saved password. |  | default,choices

- notes | Notes | Any notes for later? | Free text, shown in komando show and to AI agents. Never put a password here. |  | optional,advanced
### add form: Databases / Snowflake
title: Add a Snowflake database
- name | Name | What do you want to call this database? | A short name you type later, like komando test analytics. Letters, digits, dot, dash, underscore. | analytics | check
- account | Account | What is the account identifier? | In Snowsight: your name at the bottom left, Account, View account details. It is also the first part of your link, before .snowflakecomputing.com. | myorg-myaccount | check
- user | User | Which Snowflake user do you log in as? | A user for komando that may only read is safest. Names are usually in capitals. | APP_RO | check
- login | Login | How does this user log in? | Snowflake takes no passwords here: a key pair or a programmatic access token. Browser sign-in (SSO) does not work. |  | default,choices
- keyfile | Key file | Where is the private key file? | A .p8 or .pem file without a passphrase. komando reads it each time, so leave it where it is. | ~/keys/rsa_key.p8 | show,check
- secret | Saved key | Which saved secret holds the key or the token? | A name from komando secret list, or where it is kept, like secret:NAME or env:VAR. |  | free,choices,show,check
- warehouse | Warehouse | Which warehouse runs the queries? | Most queries need one. Empty is fine for a first test. | REPORTING | optional,check
- database | Database | Which database should commands use? | Empty for none: then write DATABASE.SCHEMA.TABLE in queries. | ANALYTICS | optional,check
- schema | Schema | Which schema inside it? | Empty for none. | PUBLIC | optional,show,check
- role | Role | Which role should komando use? | Best a role that may only read. Empty uses the user's default role. | ANALYST_RO | optional,check
- protected | Production | Can a mistake on this database hurt real users or real data? | Production: komando asks you before every change, and an AI agent needs your yes in a window. |  | default,choices
- via | Reached | How does this computer reach the database? | Pick a server when the database only answers on that server or inside its network. |  | advanced,default,choices,when
- group | Group | Put it in a group? | A group lets one command reach many, like komando test @web. Empty for none. | web | optional,advanced,check
- notes | Notes | Any notes for later? | Free text, shown in komando show and to AI agents. Never put a password here. |  | optional,advanced
### add form: Databases / Google BigQuery
title: Add a Google BigQuery database
- name | Name | What do you want to call this database? | A short name you type later, like komando test warehouse. Letters, digits, dot, dash, underscore. | warehouse | check
- project | Project | Which Google Cloud project runs the queries? | The project ID (not its name), from the project picker in the Google Cloud console. Queries are billed to it. | my-project | check
- dataset | Dataset | Which dataset should table names use? | Then orders means analytics.orders. Empty: write DATASET.TABLE in queries. | analytics | optional,check
- location | Location | Where is the data kept? | EU, US or a region like europe-west1, as the dataset's details show. Empty lets BigQuery find it from the tables. | EU | optional,check
- login | Login | How does komando log in to Google Cloud? | No password: your Google login. A service account is a login for programs; its key is a JSON file you download once. |  | default,choices
- keyfile | Key file | Where is the key file? | The JSON file from IAM, Service accounts, Keys. komando reads it each time, so leave it where it is. | ~/keys/komando-sa.json | show,check
- protected | Production | Can a mistake on this database hurt real users or real data? | Production: komando asks you before every change, and an AI agent needs your yes in a window. |  | default,choices
- via | Reached | How does this computer reach the database? | Pick a server when the database only answers on that server or inside its network. |  | advanced,default,choices,when
- group | Group | Put it in a group? | A group lets one command reach many, like komando test @web. Empty for none. | web | optional,advanced,check
- notes | Notes | Any notes for later? | Free text, shown in komando show and to AI agents. Never put a password here. |  | optional,advanced

### add form: Caches / Redis or Valkey
title: Add a Redis cache
- name | Name | What do you want to call this cache? | A short name you type later, like komando test shop-cache. Letters, digits, dot, dash, underscore. | shop-cache | check

- secret | Saved password | Which saved secret holds the password? | A name from komando secret list, or where it is kept, like secret:NAME or env:VAR. |  | free,choices,show,check

- tlsvia | Encryption | Does the cache use TLS (an encrypted connection)? | Usually not through a server. Yes only when the cache itself asks for TLS. |  | advanced,default,choices,show
- user | User | Which user do you log in as? | Only for Redis 6 or newer with ACL users. Empty when you only have a password. | app | optional,advanced,check
- setup | Setup | How is Redis set up? |  |  | advanced,default,choices
- db | Database number | Which database number? | Redis has numbered databases, 0 to 15. Apps almost always use 0. |  | optional,advanced,default,show,check
- master | Master name | What is the master's name at the Sentinels? | The name in sentinel.conf, on the line sentinel monitor NAME ... | mymaster | advanced,show,check
- sentinels | Other Sentinels | Other Sentinel addresses? | Comma separated, tried when the first one does not answer. Empty for none. | 10.0.0.8, 10.0.0.9:26379 | optional,advanced,show,check
- sentinelauth | Sentinel login | Do the Sentinels need the same login as Redis? | Only when the Sentinels themselves have a password. |  | advanced,default,choices,show
- ca | CA certificate | Which saved CA certificate should komando trust? | Only for a certificate from your own CA. Save it first: komando secret set NAME < ca.crt. Empty for none. |  | optional,advanced,free,choices,show,check

- keyid | Access key ID | What is the access key ID? | The public half of the key (Backblaze calls it keyID). When the command asks "Password for" with the name you gave, paste the secret half; it stays hidden. | AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE | show,check

- resolve | Fixed IP | Connect to a fixed IP address instead of looking up the name? | Only when the address has no DNS entry or a wrong one. The certificate is still checked against the name. | 203.0.113.10 or 203.0.113.10:9000 | optional,advanced,show,check

### add form: Clusters / Docker Swarm
title: Add a Docker Swarm
- name | Name | What do you want to call this swarm manager? | A short name you type later, like komando test swarm1. Letters, digits, dot, dash, underscore. | swarm1 | check

- os | System | What does the server run? | Windows servers run commands in PowerShell; everything else is treated like Linux. |  | default,choices

- port | Port | Which SSH port does it use? | Almost always 22. Change it only if your provider gave you another number. |  | default,show,check
- winrmtls | Encryption | How does WinRM encrypt the connection? | Pick the first unless komando test says the certificate is not trusted. A certificate from your company's CA: keep the first and see https://github.com/sgnd/komando/blob/main/docs/features/windows.md. |  | default,choices,show
- winrmport | Port | Which WinRM port does it use? | Almost always 5986 for HTTPS and 5985 for HTTP. |  | default,show,check
- login | Login | How do you log in? | Not sure? Pick the first: komando tries your keys and asks for a password if none works. |  | default,choices,show
- identity | Key file | Where is the key file? | The private key file, often ending in .pem. Not the .pub file. | ~/Downloads/my-vps.pem | show,check
- key | Key | Which of your komando keys? |  |  | choices,show
- protected | Production | Can a mistake on this server hurt real users or real data? | Production: komando asks you before every change, and an AI agent needs your yes in a window. |  | default,choices
- via | Jump host | Through another server (a jump host)? | Pick a server or VPN when this server only answers from inside that network. |  | advanced,default,choices
- code | One-time code | Does it also ask for a one-time code when you log in? | A 6-digit code from an app like Google Authenticator. Most servers do not. |  | advanced,default,choices,show
- group | Group | Put it in a group? | A group lets one command reach many, like komando test @web. Empty for none. | web | optional,advanced,check
- notes | Notes | Any notes for later? | Free text, shown in komando show and to AI agents. Never put a password here. |  | optional,advanced

- ca | CA certificate | Which saved secret holds the CA certificate? | The CA certificate you stored with komando secret set NAME < ca.crt. |  | advanced,free,choices,show,check
- resolve | Use IP | Connect to another IP than DNS gives? (leave empty to use DNS) | Only for a registry whose name is not in DNS yet. The certificate is still checked against the name. | 203.0.113.10 or 203.0.113.10:8443 | optional,advanced,show,check

- mfa | Extra sign-in step | After the password, does logging in need one more step? | With an extra step you connect it yourself with komando vpn up; later commands reuse that connection. |  | default,choices,show

- group | Group | Put it in a group? | A group lets one command reach many, like komando test @web. Empty for none. | web | optional,advanced,check
- notes | Notes | Any notes for later? | Free text, shown in komando show and to AI agents. Never put a password here. |  | optional,advanced
### add form: VPN / Cisco AnyConnect
title: Add a Cisco AnyConnect VPN
- name | Name | What do you want to call this VPN? | A short name you type later, like komando test client-x. Letters, digits, dot, dash, underscore. | client-x | check

### add form: VPN / L2TP/IPsec
title: Add an L2TP/IPsec VPN
- name | Name | What do you want to call this VPN? | A short name you type later, like komando test office. Letters, digits, dot, dash, underscore. | office | check
- server | Server | What is the VPN server's address? | A host name or IP address from your admin, or from the VPN settings on your phone or laptop. | vpn.example.com | addr,check
- psk | Shared secret | How should komando get the shared secret (pre-shared key)? | One password for the whole office, often called IPsec secret or PSK. Your admin gives it to you. |  | default,choices
- pskref | Kept in | Where is it kept? | A reference, never the secret itself: op://Work/VPN/password (1Password), bw://item (Bitwarden), env:VPN_PASS (a variable). | op://Work/VPN/password | show,check
- user | User | What is your VPN user name? | Your own login on the VPN, from your admin. | budi | check
- pass | Password | How should komando get your VPN password? | The password is never shown and never written in the command. |  | default,choices,show
- ref | Kept in | Where is it kept? | A reference, never the secret itself: op://Work/VPN/password (1Password), bw://item (Bitwarden), env:VPN_PASS (a variable). | op://Work/VPN/password | show,check
- check | Test address | Which address can only be reached through this VPN? (optional) | An address and port inside the private network, like a server's private IP and port 22. komando connects to it to see that the VPN works. Enter skips it. | 10.0.0.5:22 | optional,check
- legacy | Old encryption | Is it an old server that needs old, weak encryption (3DES)? | Only when connecting fails and your admin says the server is old. komando asks you to confirm it. |  | advanced,default,choices
- pap | Weak login | Does the old server only take a weak login (PAP, CHAP-MD5 or none)? | These do not prove the server is real, and PAP hands it your password itself. Only when your admin says so; komando asks you to confirm it. |  | advanced,default,choices
- group | Group | Put it in a group? | A group lets one command reach many, like komando test @web. Empty for none. | web | optional,advanced,check
- notes | Notes | Any notes for later? | Free text, shown in komando show and to AI agents. Never put a password here. |  | optional,advanced

### add form: VPN / IKEv2
title: Add an IKEv2 VPN
- name | Name | What do you want to call this VPN? | A short name you type later, like komando test office. Letters, digits, dot, dash, underscore. | office | check
- server | Server | What is the VPN server's address? | A host name or IP address from your admin, or from the VPN settings on your phone or laptop. | vpn.example.com | addr,check
- auth | Login | How do you log in? |  |  | default,choices
- psk | Shared secret | How should komando get the shared secret (pre-shared key)? | Your admin gives it to you; it is often called PSK. |  | default,choices,show
- pskref | Kept in | Where is it kept? | A reference, never the secret itself: op://Work/VPN/password (1Password), bw://item (Bitwarden), env:VPN_PASS (a variable). | op://Work/VPN/password | show,check
- user | User | What is your VPN user name? | Your own login on the VPN. | budi | show,check
- pass | Password | How should komando get your VPN password? | The password is never shown and never written in the command. |  | default,choices,show
- ref | Kept in | Where is it kept? | A reference, never the secret itself: op://Work/VPN/password (1Password), bw://item (Bitwarden), env:VPN_PASS (a variable). | op://Work/VPN/password | show,check
- check | Test address | Which address can only be reached through this VPN? (optional) | An address and port inside the private network, like a server's private IP and port 22. komando connects to it to see that the VPN works. Enter skips it. | 10.0.0.5:22 | optional,check
- ca | Certificate | Did your admin give you the server's certificate file? | A .pem or .crt file. Empty when the server has a normal public certificate. | ~/Downloads/vpn-ca.pem | optional,advanced,check
- id | Your identity | Does the server know you by another name than your user name? | Only when your admin gives you an identity. Empty uses your user name. | budi@example.com | optional,advanced
- remoteid | Server identity | Does the server have another name than its address? | Only when your admin gives you one. Empty uses the server address. | vpn.example.com | optional,advanced
- group | Group | Put it in a group? | A group lets one command reach many, like komando test @web. Empty for none. | web | optional,advanced,check
- notes | Notes | Any notes for later? | Free text, shown in komando show and to AI agents. Never put a password here. |  | optional,advanced
